_paths_comment: Portable paths: ${HOUFIN_DATA}/${HOUFIN_PROCESSED} expand at load (src/config_utils.py; default <repo>/data and <repo>/data/processed locally, override via env on HPC). NOTE: the age-model fit + path-features pipeline is a later milestone; these paths are provisional (they consume the encoder cube + BBS produced upstream).
_disease_arrival_map_comment: Per-pixel first-affected-breeding-season for House Finch mycoplasmal conjunctivitis, on the model grid. Built by scripts/build_disease_arrival_map.py from the documented 1994-2006 spread history (there is no published raster). Consumed by model_inputs.py as the onset gate for the K depression -- see src/model/age_fields.py.

kernel_contract._comment: The encoder supplies an uncentered 64-D Nyström feature map; model ingestion explicitly retains the first latent_dim=16 eigenfeatures by default to fit VRAM. Conditional on each w_scale, iid coefficients over those retained features imply Cov[H(x),H(x')|w_scale] = w_scale^2 Z_r(x)·Z_r(x'), the configured rank-r approximation to the original Ružička kernel. Truncation must be config-driven and recorded, never silent.

dispersal._comment: Single source of truth shared by Z_disp preparation and the forward model; resolved in exactly one place, build_kernels.dispersal_spec. Do not duplicate these boundaries in code.
dispersal._radial_splits_comment: juvenile_radial_splits_km accepts either an explicit list of km boundaries (must start at 0.0 and end >=1e8) or the string "derive", which computes equal-mass radial bands (quantiles, default terciles, overridable via juvenile_radial_split_quantiles) for whatever juvenile_mdd_km is set. The pinned list below is NOT a set of quantiles of the 330 km kernel: it is log-spaced band edges from 50 to 1500 km, produced by a get_log_spaced_splits(50,1500,3) helper that no longer exists, and it does NOT move with juvenile_mdd_km -- at mdd=150 the three cohorts hold 67/28/4% of the dispersal mass, at 400 they hold 32/41/27%. It is retained here only for artifact compatibility: the 124-year Z_disp cube on TACC was built under these exact literals, and ingest compares the resolved dispersal dict for exact equality. New work (and every dispersal sweep point) should use "derive".
dispersal._path_comment: Z_disp is intentionally a land-conditioned neighborhood/path summary: at each fractional displacement, water/nodata is excluded and the remaining land contribution is normalized. It is not a literal trajectory hazard through water.

age_structure_prior._comment: Resolution-invariant weak local-age-structure regularizer. We average log Beta density over land cell-years, then multiply by effective_sites, instead of treating every grid cell/year as an independent prior observation. This is a distributional belief about a representative local cell, not a prior on the domain-wide mean.

population_model._comment: Mechanistic/data-scale constants persisted into model-input metadata; no hidden grid or invasion constants in ingestion code.
population_model._scale_comment: THE GAUGE. population_scale_route_counts_per_relative_unit converts model density to the mean of a BBS route count (expected_obs = density * this). It is a SAMPLER-CONDITIONING choice, not biology: the likelihood is EXACTLY invariant under (K -> cK, initpop -> c*initpop, inv_pop -> c*inv_pop, allee_gamma -> allee_gamma/c, this -> this/c), because K enters the forward sim only as N/K and the Allee term only as allee_gamma*N and allee_gamma*K. Set from the q95 of MODERN (>2000) per-GRID-CELL mean House Finch route counts, computed over cells rather than observations because BBS sampling density is spatially biased. Empirically q95 = 19.4, rounded to 20. The previous value, 210, was ~the MAX per-cell mean, which is why it conditioned badly: normalizing by an extreme put the typical occupied cell at density 0.010 and the median cell at 0.003, i.e. all the mass in the bottom 1% of [0,1]. At 20 the occupied bulk lands in [0.1, 1] (typical occupied cell 0.11, q90 0.81) with ~5% of cells above 1, which is harmless since density is not a probability. RULE: because this is a free gauge choice, EVERY absolute-scale prior must be declared in ROUTE-COUNT units and divided by it at one boundary, so changing it cannot change any prior's meaning. n50 already followed this convention; capacity_level, initpop, and the invasion pulse now do too.
population_model._disease_prior_comment: The mycoplasmal-conjunctivitis effect on carrying capacity, as a STRUCTURED hypothesis: K = K_base * (1 - severity(x) * onset_gate(x,t) * (1 - recovery(t - arrival))). See src/model/age_fields.py for the formulation and src/model/age_priors.py for the priors. This replaces a generic 967-coefficient spatiotemporal cosine field (the old st_basis_space/time_frequencies) which was subtracted from K's PRE-softplus argument. That design failed two ways: (1) fitted K sits where softplus is effectively exp(), so an additive penalty was an unbounded MULTIPLICATIVE one -- a depression of 3.5 removed 97% of K -- and it annihilated carrying capacity across the entire eastern US rather than rescaling it; (2) being the model's only non-covariate spatial degree of freedom, with K ~multiplicative on predicted abundance, it absorbed every kind of spatial misfit rather than disease alone. The structured form is bounded by construction (a fraction in (0,1) can never zero K out), uses ~55 free parameters instead of 967, and every parameter states a testable claim. Frequencies are per-AXIS over the grid extent: severity/lag space=4 -> ~900km half-wavelength N-S, ~1500km E-W, i.e. deliberately coarse regional structure (east vs west vs plains), not habitat-scale detail.
population_model._capacity_level_comment: Prior on K's continental LEVEL, declared in expected BBS route counts (see _scale_comment: divided by the gauge in code, so this number means the same thing whatever the gauge is). Replaces alpha_k ~ Normal(0.5, 0.5), which was stated in relative units and therefore asserted -- unnoticed -- that every cell's capacity equals softplus(0.5)*210 = 205 counts, i.e. ~97% of the highest route counts ever recorded. The data want ~2 counts, so that prior sat 7 SDs from the fit, and every term able to lower K (disease severity, the H_k deviation, the continental trend) got recruited as a level reducer and saturated. That is why capping each one in turn only moved the pressure. Centered on the TYPICAL OCCUPIED cell: median 2.1 counts, geometric mean 1.87 -- the two agree, so the anchor is robust. LogNormal because a positive scale wants a multiplicative prior; log_sd 0.8 gives a 5-95% span of ~[0.6, 8] counts. Empty cells are expected to be empty for NICHE reasons (lambda < 1 via survival/fecundity), not because capacity is low there.
population_model._initpop_comment: The t=0 (1902) native-range seed, in expected BBS route counts, converted through the gauge in model_inputs. Derived from the pre-1970 western occupied-cell distribution, which bbs.py prints at ingest so these can be re-checked: q10 1.0, q25 3.0, q50 9.5, q75 35.5, q90 61.5 counts. core = the MEDIAN native occupied cell (9.5); margin = q25 (3.0). An earlier version used the median of the >75th-percentile core-hull cells (61 counts) which was far too high: that is the q90 of the native distribution applied UNIFORMLY across a rasterized convex hull containing many much sparser cells, and it sat at 97% of the maximum reachable K (level 2.1 x fold 30 = 63), so most core cells would have started above their own carrying capacity and immediately crashed. At 9.5 the core seed is 4.5x the capacity level -- above it, since the native range was at equilibrium, but comfortably inside the fold range. Note these seed 1902, not 1966: BBS starts in 1966, so pre-1970 counts are a proxy for the historical native range, not a measurement of it.
population_model._invasion_pulse_comment: The 1940 NYC release, declared in expected BBS route counts and converted through the gauge like every other absolute-scale prior. Was softplus(Normal(-2,1)) in relative units, i.e. ~27 counts at the old gauge of 210 -- a founding population larger than a typical modern occupied cell, which is not what a release of a few dozen escaped cage birds looks like. LogNormal median 1.0 count with log_sd 1.0 spans ~0.14 to 7 counts.
population_model._manifold_comment: Correlated weights for the THREE demographic manifolds: H_s (survival, drives Sa/Sj/Q), H_r (reproduction, drives Fmax), H_k (capacity, drives K). K used to reuse H_r outright, i.e. an implicit correlation of exactly 1.0, which meant K's spatial pattern could differ from Fmax's ONLY through the disease term -- so every real disagreement between 'where reproduction is good' and 'where birds are abundant' had to be spelled 'disease', and the disease term saturated. Parameterized as one shared habitat-quality factor: beta_j = s_j * (h_j*f + sqrt(1-h_j^2)*eps_j) with f, eps iid across features. That makes Var(beta_j) = s_j^2 and Corr(j,k) = h_j*h_k EXACTLY, positive-definite for free -- no Cholesky guard whose clipping would corrupt gradients, and LKJ is unusable here because its concentration parameter pushes toward ZERO correlation, the opposite of the belief. Fecundity and capacity are both productivity/resource axes, so their prior correlation is set ABOVE survival's with either: target 0.85 vs 0.70. loading_logit_scale=0.6 makes that ordering hold with ~94% prior probability while leaving the survival-fecundity 5-95% CI at [0.48, 0.83], comparable to the old rho ~ TruncatedNormal(0.7, 0.2).
population_model._k_range_comment: REPORTING threshold only -- no longer an active constraint. K is log-linear (log K_base = log(k_level) + gamma_k*H_k + trend), so the covariate term is an unbounded log-fold deviation, exactly as in any log-link GLM. A tanh clamp at this fold value was briefly in place while K kept collapsing to ~0; the real cause was alpha_k's prior sitting 7 SDs from the data (see _capacity_level_comment), and with the level stated correctly in route counts the clamp is unnecessary complication. Retained purely as the threshold metrics.json:k_range compares the REALIZED spatial fold range against, so a collapse is visible rather than hidden by a clamp. 30x is +/-2 log SD of the observed occupied-cell spread (log sd 1.72), i.e. what the data actually show; a realized range far beyond it means something is wrong.
population_model._k_trend_comment: Continental (spatially uniform) smooth time trend on K's pre-softplus argument, time-centered so alpha_k keeps the level. THIS IS A SAFETY VALVE AND A FAILURE DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A MODELED MECHANISM. It exists only because the model otherwise has NO temporal degree of freedom for capacity except the disease term, so 'modern K must be lower than 1970s K' could ONLY be expressed as disease -- and the disease term saturated at 93% severity trying. The prior is therefore very strongly concentrated on zero: budget=0.05 puts the implied K multiplier within 2.3% of 1.0 at the prior median, 7% at the 95th percentile, and 13.5% at the 99.9th (K sits near softplus's exponential regime, so multiplier ~ exp(trend)). READ IT AS: if the fitted trend moves K by more than ~10-15%, or sits more than ~3 prior SDs out (reported as k_trend.max_prior_sd_multiple in metrics.json), the model is failing to explain a real temporal signal through its mechanisms and that is the finding -- do NOT loosen this budget to accommodate it. budget=0.3 was tried first and was far too permissive: it allowed a 44% capacity swing at the 95th percentile, which makes it a working part of the model rather than an alarm. Also deliberately spatially UNIFORM with only 3 cosines over 124 years, so it cannot compete with the disease term's spatial pattern or manufacture year-to-year wiggle. It IS partially confounded with the disease severity level; what separates them is that disease onset follows the arrival map (east ~1994, west ~2005) while this trend is simultaneous everywhere.

disease_prior._severity_comment: DENSITY-DEPENDENT severity: severity(x) = severity_ceiling * K_base^n / (K_base^n + K_half^n), a Hill function of local carrying capacity. Epidemics need hosts: mass-action transmission makes R0 scale with density, and below a threshold density the pathogen cannot persist. So severity -> 0 as K_base -> 0 and -> severity_ceiling for dense populations. This matters beyond realism because the model has an Allee effect: a small absolute reduction in an already-small K can push a sparse population to local extinction, so a density-INdependent severity does disproportionate damage exactly where it is least biologically justified. Both shape parameters are FITTED, so the shape is learned: K_half is the density at half-maximum severity (in route counts, converted by the gauge) and n is the steepness -- n~1 is smooth saturation, n~3 a sharp invasion threshold. With K_half=8 counts and n=1.5 the severity across the observed occupied-cell distribution runs 1% (q25) / 6% (q50) / 22% (q75) / 37% (q90) / 48% (q99), i.e. sparse cells spared and dense cells taking the documented decline. NOTE: severity keys off K_base (potential density) rather than realized N because all demographic fields are precomputed before the forward simulation runs, so N does not exist yet; K_base is arguably the better proxy anyway, since epidemic establishment depends on sustained density rather than one year's count.
disease_prior._ceiling_comment: severity_ceiling is now LOAD-BEARING FOR IDENTIFIABILITY, not merely a bound on plausibility. K = K_base*(1 - severity(K_base)*...) must be monotone in K_base, or two different habitat qualities map to the same realized capacity. At 0.5 monotonicity holds for every n tested (min dK/dK_base = 0.100 at n=5); at 0.7 it BREAKS (slope -0.26). It also happens to match the documented ~50-60% decline, which was measured in the dense eastern populations -- exactly where this parameterization applies it. Do not raise it above ~0.6 without re-checking monotonicity.
disease_prior._mu_comment: Logit of the MODIFIER on density-dependent severity, so severity = severity_ceiling * sigmoid(mu + ...) * hill(K_base). mu_loc = logit(0.8) = 1.386 puts the prior median modifier at 0.8, i.e. a prior median severity of 0.8*0.5 = 40% in the densest populations, with mu_scale=0.5 giving a 90% CI on the modifier of about [0.62, 0.91] -> severity [31%, 46%]. That brackets the documented ~50-60% eastern decline from slightly below while leaving the ceiling as a strict bound rather than the expected value. Note the modifier is a PLAIN sigmoid: an earlier min(1, 2*sigmoid(.)) form, intended so that mu=0 meant 'no modification', put a zero-gradient clip boundary exactly at the center of mu's prior and also destroyed the land-centered field's level-neutrality.
disease_prior._field_comment: sev_field_budget is the total regional deviation the severity field may add on the logit scale (distributed as budget/sqrt(n) per coefficient); 0.5 comfortably reaches west ~25-30% vs east ~60%. lag0_scale/lag_field_budget are YEARS of onset-timing slack, continental and regional respectively -- the arrival map is a hand-built smoothed reconstruction, so its timing is coarse both overall and regionally.
disease_prior._late_comment: Severity coefficient on centered arrival year, per DECADE. Negative means populations reached later were hit less hard (the western-genetic-diversity hypothesis). TIGHTENED from scale 0.3 to 0.15 because it is now strongly COLLINEAR with the density-dependent severity above: the east is both early-arriving AND dense, the plains/west late AND sparse. In the run before density-dependence existed this coefficient went to -1.43, over 4 prior SDs, consistent with it having been doing the density job by proxy. It is kept rather than dropped because arrival order and genetic diversity are genuinely distinct from density -- if the data still want a strong b_late ALONGSIDE the density term, that is informative: it would mean arrival order carries signal density cannot explain.
disease_prior._recovery_comment: Slowly increasing resilience after local arrival: the hit decays toward severity*(1-recovery_fraction) with an e-folding time of recovery_tau years. recovery_logit_loc=-0.5 -> prior median ~38% of the hit eventually recovered, spanning 0 to ~90%.

map._comment: Continuation begins under tight priors and progressively relaxes them at absolute optimizer steps. The standard/full run uses 300 tight + 300 intermediate + 1200 nominal-prior steps (1800 total). Boundaries are independent of TOTAL_STEPS so extending/resuming a run cannot move backward. lr_decay_steps is likewise fixed across extensions; after step 900 optimization continues at the schedule's minimum learning rate.
map._log_every_comment: Steps between '[map] step ...' progress lines on stdout (the SLURM .o log). tqdm also carries the loss, but it writes a single carriage-return-rewritten line to stderr, so a running fit's loss trajectory is otherwise invisible in the log. Override per-run with HOUFIN_MAP_LOG_EVERY; 0 disables. A profile may set its own value.

quick90._comment: Fresh 90-minute development fit matching the successful accidental extension: 100 tight, 150 intermediate, and 650 nominal-prior steps (900 total). The learning-rate decay reaches its minimum at step 500 and stays there for the final 400 steps. This changes optimization only, not the final MAP objective.

runtime._comment: Production JAX jobs require a GPU and explicitly place model inputs in VRAM. HOUFIN_MODEL_INPUT_RESIDENCY=host is experimental: lax.scan is not a true differentiable host-streaming mechanism. SLURM wrappers record nvidia-smi VRAM/utilization plus host MemAvailable/SwapFree every 30 seconds.

run_names._comment: run_12: Simplified K, smaller init pop
